reconstructed_theorem_text: For all real a,b,C,epsilon with a<=b, C>=0 and epsilon>0, and every measurable f:R->R satisfying 0<=f(t)<=C for Lebesgue-almost every t in [a,b], there exists a globally C-infinity function g:R->R such that 0<g(t)<=C+epsilon for every t in [a,b], and both Lebesgue set integrals Integral_[a,b] |g(t)-f(t)| dt and Integral_[a,b] |sqrt(2*g(t))-sqrt(2*f(t))|^2 dt are strictly less than epsilon. The square roots are Lean's total real square roots.
objects: Real endpoints a,b, nonnegative bound C, positive tolerance epsilon.
Measurable f:R->R and one globally smooth witness g:R->R.
Two errors measured against the same restricted Lebesgue measure on [a,b].
domains: All functions are real-valued and defined on all R.
The square-root functions have arguments 2*g(t) and 2*f(t); the square is outside the absolute value of their difference.
quantifiers: For each admissible a,b,C,epsilon,f there exists a single g satisfying every conjunct.
The range hypothesis for f is AE on [a,b].
The positive range conclusion for g holds for every point of [a,b].
assumptions: f is globally measurable and lies in [0,C] almost everywhere on [a,b].
scopes: Both strict error inequalities use the same witness g and the same epsilon.
The second estimate concerns the squared L2 error of the square-root transforms, not an L2 norm bounded by epsilon.
No bounds on either function outside [a,b] and no everywhere nonnegativity of f are asserted.
constant_dependencies: The coefficient inside each root is exactly 2. There is no factor outside the displayed squared-difference integral.
The upper pointwise bound is exactly C+epsilon.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: Although Lean's integrals are totalized, boundedness of f AE and boundedness of g on this finite interval ensure both displayed integrands are integrable. Real.sqrt is defined at all real arguments and is zero on negative inputs; exceptional negative f-values do not invalidate the expression.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: No replacement of the AE range of f by an everywhere range; g is positive at every point of the interval.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: Both are set integrals over the ordered closed interval [a,b], with a<=b.
semantic_checks.exponents: Exactly |sqrt(2*g)-sqrt(2*f)| raised to natural power 2; the first error is |g-f| to power 1. Both integrals are <epsilon, not <=epsilon.
semantic_checks.compactness: Only finite real-interval compactness is relevant.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: a=b and C=0 are admitted; the pointwise positivity requirement on g survives a=b.
semantic_checks.absolute_continuity: g is globally smooth; no absolute-continuity assertion about f.
